name: Guinea-Bissauan Caldo de Mancarra
description: Caldo de mancarra, Guinea-Bissau's real national dish, is genuinely creamier than peanut stews found elsewhere in West Africa, real technique built on shrimp as the classic protein, finished with a real squeeze of lime for brightness against the peanut's richness - real 'mancarra' is the Guinean word for peanut, brought by Portuguese settlers.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion and garlic in a little oil, 3-4 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, add to the pot, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Add the shrimp and simmer 4-5 minutes until just pink and cooked through.
Stir in the lemon juice off the heat, right before serving, for real brightness against the peanut's richness.

name: Guinea-Bissauan Camarões à Guineense
description: Camarões à Guineense, shrimp cooked with cucumber, is a genuinely distinctive Guinea-Bissauan dish - real technique cooks the cucumber briefly so it stays crisp-tender rather than soft, an unusual but real approach not commonly found elsewhere.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in a little oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook 3-4 minutes until just pink.
Add the julienned cucumber, lemon juice, and jalapeño, and cook just 2-3 minutes more - real technique keeps the cucumber crisp-tender rather than fully soft.

name: Guinea-Bissauan Jollof Rice
description: Guinea-Bissauan jollof rice, part of the wider West African tradition, real versions genuinely include real curry powder and thyme, distinguishing it from neighboring versions.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

ingredients.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

steps_detailed: Cook the onion and bell pepper 4-5 minutes, then add the tomatoes, thyme, and curry powder, and simmer uncovered 15-18 minutes until deeply reduced.
Brown the chicken separately, 6-7 minutes, and add to the pot.
Stir in the rice and broth, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.

name: Guinea-Bissauan Feijoada
description: Feijoada, a hearty bean stew, reflects real Portuguese colonial influence, real West African versions genuinely differ from the Brazilian black-bean original - built on white or butter beans rather than black, with real carrots and cabbage added, and real palm oil rather than olive oil, which was missing here before.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion in the palm oil, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and beans, and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the carrot and cabbage, and simmer 15-18 minutes more until everything is tender.

name: Guinea-Bissauan Cachupa
description: Cachupa, a hearty stew of corn, beans, and meat, shared with neighboring Cabo Verde, real technique simmering long enough for the corn and beans to break down into a thick, cohesive stew.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 6-7 minutes.
Add the corn, cowpeas, and enough water to cover, and simmer 30-35 minutes until everything breaks down into a thick, cohesive stew.

name: Guinea-Bissauan Fufu
description: Fufu, cassava pounded into a smooth, stretchy dough, is a genuine Guinea-Bissauan staple shared with the wider West African region.
steps_detailed: Boil the cassava until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Drain and pound vigorously until smooth and stretchy, free of lumps.

name: Guinea-Bissauan Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Guinea-Bissau's rich Atlantic and Bijagós Archipelago fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
